neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: NORMAL. No facial weakness, no ptosis, no ophthalmoplegia.
neurological_exam.motor: NORMAL: 5/5 throughout bilateral upper and lower extremities. No weakness detectable on formal testing.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral hand tingling and mild bilateral distal foot tingling. Vibration slightly reduced at bilateral great toes.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Absent bilateral Achilles reflexes. Trace bilateral patellar. Trace bilateral brachioradialis. Absent bilateral biceps and triceps. GLOBAL AREFLEXIA in setting of normal strength.
neurological_exam.coordination: Normal finger-to-nose. Normal heel-to-shin. Normal gait on wide base.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly unsteady — wide-based gait but able to walk. Slight difficulty with tandem gait.
neurological_exam.additional: FVC: 3.4 L (predicted 3.8 L — 89%). NIF: -52 cmH2O. Currently normal. NCS was ordered.

patient.chief_complaint: Three-day bilateral tingling, bilateral areflexia, and mild gait unsteadiness in a 22-year-old with no weakness — 2 weeks after Campylobacter gastroenteritis.
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. B. is a 22-year-old college student presenting to the ED with a 3-day history of bilateral tingling in her hands and feet. She had a clear Campylobacter gastroenteritis 2 weeks ago, confirmed by stool culture at a student health center. She recovered fully. Three days ago she developed bilateral hand and foot tingling. Yesterday she noticed her reflexes seemed absent when she tested them with her roommate (nursing student). She reports very mild gait unsteadiness but denies frank weakness — she walked to the ED. She has no facial symptoms, no diplopia, no dysphagia. She is very anxious. The ED physician considered a functional neurological disorder given the absence of objective weakness. The key diagnostic question: does early-stage GBS (areflexia + paresthesias without weakness) require treatment and admission, or can she be discharged?

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: CRP 12.4 mg/L (H), ESR 32 mm/hr (H), Campylobacter jejuni IgM Positive  (H), Anti-GM1 IgG Positive (titer 1:80)  (H).

findings.finding: DML 5.6 ms (prolonged; normal <4.2); CV 42 m/s (borderline); CMAP 5.2 mV (normal)
DML 6.8 ms (prolonged); CV 38 m/s (reduced); CMAP 4.8 mV (normal)
SNAP absent bilaterally — CRITICAL: this is early GBS sentinel finding
ABSENT in bilateral peroneal and median — proximal demyelination present
Normal insertional activity, normal motor unit recruitment bilaterally — no denervation (consistent with early AIDP before axonal injury)

quantitative_data.pattern: Early AIDP — proximal demyelination with absent F-waves/H-reflex, absent sensory SNAPs, borderline motor changes

specialized_test.impression: Early AIDP meeting electrodiagnostic criteria despite absence of clinical weakness. Prolonged distal motor latencies, absent F-waves, absent H-reflex, and absent sural SNAPs are the earliest NCS features of GBS. The preserved CMAP amplitudes indicate no axonal injury yet — this is truly early disease.
recommended_actions: ADMIT for close monitoring — GBS in the early phase will progress

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 130 mmH2O. WBC: 1 cell/mm3 (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 34 mg/dL (normal — upper limit 45 mg/dL). Glucose: 62 mg/dL (ratio 0.69). Gram stain: No organisms.

findings.finding: Subtle enhancement of cauda equina nerve roots — mildly thickened and enhancing on post-gadolinium images
No cord signal abnormality — no myelitis

output.impression: Early cauda equina nerve root enhancement consistent with early GBS/AIDP. No spinal cord abnormality — excludes myelitis. Subtle nerve root changes are consistent with very early GBS.

output.query: GBS early treatment IVIG when to initiate areflexia without weakness

results.title: GBS treatment timing
results.finding: IVIG is most effective when started within 2 weeks of symptom onset; early GBS (areflexia without weakness) is treated to prevent progression to respiratory failure

results.title: GBS natural history
results.finding: GBS progresses for 2-4 weeks; 30% of patients require mechanical ventilation; early mild presentation can rapidly worsen

results.title: Brighton criteria for GBS
results.finding: Brighton level 1 criteria: bilateral flaccid limb weakness + decreased DTRs in weak limbs + symptom progression <12 weeks + no alternative diagnosis; NCS confirmation level 1

output.summary: Early GBS (areflexia without weakness) should be treated and admitted for monitoring. IVIG is most effective within 2 weeks. GBS can progress rapidly from mild sensory symptoms to respiratory failure. Do not discharge patients with confirmed early GBS.

output.impression: Normal cardiac monitoring at early GBS stage. Continue monitoring as autonomic dysfunction can develop.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AIDP — early presentation (day 3, areflexia without weakness)

differential.key_features: NCS shows objective early AIDP changes; absent SNAPs and absent F-waves are not functional
Objective NCS findings, Campylobacter serology positive, anti-GM1 IgG positive
B12 normal; acute 3-day onset is not B12 deficiency

optimal_actions.action: Urgent NCS/EMG — do not dismiss early GBS without electrophysiology
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Early AIDP — absent F-waves, absent SNAPs, prolonged DMLs despite normal strength
Campylobacter IgM positive; anti-GM1 IgG positive
Normal early — CSF protein may not yet be elevated at day 3

optimal_actions.action: ADMIT for monitoring — do NOT discharge despite no weakness
Initiate IVIG — early treatment prevents progression

critical_actions: DO NOT DISCHARGE — early GBS without weakness can progress to respiratory failure within days
Admit for serial respiratory monitoring every 4-6 hours
Normal CSF does NOT exclude GBS at day 3 — protein peaks at 2-4 weeks
Initiate IVIG early — most effective within first 2 weeks
Continuous cardiac telemetry — autonomic involvement can develop
contraindicated_actions: Discharging patient with confirmed early NCS changes and areflexia — dangerous
Diagnosing as functional disorder without NCS confirmation
Delaying IVIG until weakness develops — preventable if treated early
key_reasoning_points: The diagnostic puzzle: this is GBS day 3 — symptoms are sensory only with areflexia and NO weakness — this is the critical window for early treatment
Normal CSF is expected in early GBS — albumino-cytologic dissociation peaks at 2-4 weeks; do not exclude GBS based on normal early CSF
NCS shows objective early changes (absent F-waves, absent SNAPs) even when patient has no weakness — this is the earliest stage
GBS can go from sensory symptoms to respiratory failure in 1-2 weeks — early admission and IVIG is critical
Absent F-waves and H-reflex are the EARLIEST NCS findings in GBS — present before clinical weakness

red_herrings.intended_effect: Prompt agent to consider non-GBS diagnosis (functional, anxiety) due to absence of expected weakness
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: GBS day 3 — sensory and areflexia precede weakness; NCS confirms early AIDP; admit and treat
